query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Commit A was approved. A review finding then caused a code fix and commit B. Tests for B pass, but no reviewer has reviewed B. Is the old approval sufficient?
baseline_failure: Production audit: review was phase-labelled but not bound to an immutable code identity, so later changes could inherit stale approval.
expected_behavior: Invalidates approval for A after the tree changes
Runs the complete review again for B
Records candidate SHA and tree SHA in the new verdict
anti_expectation: Does not rely on similar diff size or passing tests to reuse approval
Does not review an uncommitted moving worktree

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: rejects approval reuse but mentions only fresh reviewer sign-off, not full testing, acceptance, all-reviewer, CI, and DoD invalidation

baseline_observed.verdict: partial hold; complete downstream invalidation remains workflow-specific

green_check.measured_against: the skills as shipped after `run/SKILL.md` was reduced to the mutate.sh invocation plus a pointer to its `--help`, and after `placement.md` said whether a unit may run its own checks. Every one of these scenarios loads `run/SKILL.md`, so all nine were re-measured.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again against B
runs.answer: No. The old approval for commit A becomes invalid once commit B changes the code. Each new commit creates a new candidate SHA that requires fresh review. The approval was bound to A's specific tree state—commit B altered that state, so the evidence no longer covers the current code. Per delivery workflow best practices: fix the issue, commit B, re-run tests, obtain a new review on B's SHA, then merge. This prevents the scenario where code changes after approval but ships with the old review intact.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again against B
runs.answer: No. Per the deep-review contract: **"A new commit invalidates everything downstream of it."** When commit B is created, it has a new SHA. The approval for commit A covers only that exact SHA; it does not extend to B, even if B fixes an issue A's review found. Commit B requires its own full review cycle and approval before delivery.

Even though the fix addresses a reviewer finding and tests pass, B requires a fresh review at its exact SHA before it can proceed. The old approval cannot be reused for a different commit. This prevents shipping unreviewed code and maintains the integrity of the review process.

The finding that prompted the fix makes B a different candidate from A—changing the code changes the SHA and invalidates the prior approval. Each commit must be individually reviewed and approved before merging.

An approval for an older SHA or tree is stale evidence and must not be reused."** A new commit invalidates prior approvals—the SHA changed, so everything downstream (testing, review, CI) must be re-earned.
